teach_overlay.detail: Inked comparison diagram on period paper showing conventional carmine stain (100% of neurons stained = unreadable tangled mat) vs Camillo Golgi's 1873 silver chromate 'black reaction' (1%–5% of neurons stained stark black on a clear yellow background)
teach_overlay.scale: by staining only one to five cells out of every hundred, Golgi's silver reaction made single trees visible inside the densest forest in nature
